text:
Detroit and Edmonton both arrive after losing on Saturday. The Red Wings fell 4-1 at CGY despite holding 65% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and they sit 3-1-1 over their last five without Mason Appleton and Marco Kasper. The Oilers' three-game winning streak ended in a 7-2 loss to TOR, and they're without Mattias Ekholm. Ryan Shea has moved in beside Bouchard, and Shakir Mukhamadullin is up to 17:28 a night from 12:05. Our model has it almost even, 3.04 expected goals for DET and 3.02 for EDM.

Edmonton's results run ahead of its chances (a +9 goal difference on +3.6 expected), while Detroit has been better than its -4 goal difference, held back by finishing. At five on five, DET has taken 53% of the expected goals and EDM 49%. The special-teams matchup to watch is EDM's power play (0.91 expected goals a game) against DET's penalty kill (0.78), and Detroit takes 4.5 penalties a game. Both projected goalies are struggling: John Gibson (DET) is 4.3 goals saved above expected below par this season, Tristan Jarry (EDM) 6.6 below, though Gibson was 10.1 above last year and Jarry 4.2 below.

Connor McDavid has an 11-game point streak and is 92% to get a point in our model. Leon Draisaitl has goals in six straight, and 22 points in ten games when we'd expect about 15. For Detroit, Alex DeBrincat (38% to score) reached 300 career goals in Seattle on Oct. 20, and Lucas Raymond is heating up, per Yahoo Sports.
